checks: Original candidate 8b5860c585f8735a at its pinned digest, §2, (3) and the corollary, contains the claim. The reviewed theorem keeps 3≤m≤D+1 and makes the positive minimum explicit for the three-cap overlap consequence.

For a fixed proper inclusion-minimal j-cap subcover, 23a563a735c07c25 first gives dimension min(ρ,j−1); weakening its coefficient gives the j−1 version. This includes j=1: one cap has mass V and γ_0=1. For q>0, differentiating q log(1+1/q) gives log(1+1/q)−1/(q+1)>0, so γ_q strictly decreases, with γ_0>γ_1. As α>0 and j−1<r, the coefficient change to 1/γ_r is strictly positive; omitted hinge terms are nonnegative.

With all m caps minimal, proper normals give 1≤ρ≤m. If ρ<r then min(ρ,m−1)=ρ and the same strict coefficient comparison applies to the entire family. If ρ=m then the normals are independent and m≤D automatically, so the strict independent-normal theorem applies at every α>0. In the boundary case m=D+1 that rank is impossible. The only surviving rank is r=m−1.

At rank r, each halfspace is the inverse image of a proper closed halfspace in the normal span. Each point of the projected body has a lift in K, so the projected family covers it, and the pushforward definition preserves total mass and every cap mass. The projected body is full dimensional in the span. For D>r the section argument in 23a563a735c07c25 gives a log-concave density positive on the projected interior; if D=r the density is the uniform indicator. The parent log-concave theorem now applies to exactly r+1 proper caps, with r≥2, in both directions.

At m=3 and a=min_i A_i>0, every A_i−a is nonnegative even under ties, and (1/γ_2)=(3/2)^2=9/4. Thus the equality equation is exactly Σ_i A_i−V=(3−9/4)a=(3/4)a. No such rigidity is inferred at a=0: a proper halfspace can contain all of K and two others can miss K, giving overlap equality with zero minimum.
